Bucket 1 had zero judge errors in our sample.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="A4.SS3.SSS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The dominant failure mode in bucket 3 is taboo-topic over-fire: when a harmful prompt elicits a response that contains the requested harmful content (often very explicit step-by-step instructions for child pornography production, mass shootings, identity theft, ethnic genocide justification, or phishing emails) but wraps it in a moralising disclaimer (<span id="A4.SS3.SSS4.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">“This is illegal and morally reprehensible”</span>, <span id="A4.SS3.SSS4.p3.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">“It is important to note that…”</span>), the judge tends to apply <span id="A4.SS3.SSS4.p3.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">refusal_status=refusing</span> and tag <span id="A4.SS3.SSS4.p3.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">unethical_or_illegal</span>—contradicting the judge’s own decision tree, which explicitly states that harmful content is not in itself a refusal. The implication is substantial: of the <math id="A4.SS3.SSS4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2{,}959" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2,959</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2{,}959</annotation></semantics></math> Direction A cases, approximately <math id="A4.SS3.SSS4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1{,}794" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1,794</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1{,}794</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="A4.SS3.SSS4.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="61\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>61</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">61\%</annotation></semantics></math>) are judge over-fires rather than substring under-counts (<math id="A4.SS3.SSS4.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="95\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>95</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">95\%</annotation></semantics></math> CI <math id="A4.SS3.SSS4.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[1{,}268,2{,}283]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>1,268</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>283</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[1{,}268,2{,}283]</annotation></semantics></math>). On the harmful-prompt subset (<math id="A4.SS3.SSS4.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=12{,}000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12,000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=12{,}000</annotation></semantics></math>) this inflates the judge’s apparent refusal rate by roughly <math id="A4.SS3.SSS4.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>15</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15</annotation></semantics></math> percentage points.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS3.SSS5" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">D.3.5 </span>Bracketing the true refusal rate</h4>

<div id="A4.SS3.SSS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Both methods exhibit asymmetric biases on harmful prompts, but the calibrated audit shows the biases are not of comparable magnitude. Substring matching is biased toward false negatives, missing opposite-task substitutions and a small number of non-canonical refusal phrasings (<math id="A4.SS3.SSS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim 5</annotation></semantics></math> p.p.) and over-counting initial-refusal-then-compliance patterns (<math id="A4.SS3.SSS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim 3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim 3</annotation></semantics></math> p.p. via Direction B), for a net bias close to zero. The LLM judge is biased toward false positives of substantially larger magnitude (approximately <math id="A4.SS3.SSS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+15</annotation></semantics></math> p.p. from taboo-topic over-fire). Translating these into bounds on the true refusal rate <math id="A4.SS3.SSS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> on harmful prompts:</p>
<table id="A4.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A4.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\hat{r}_{\text{sub}}+0.05\;\lesssim\;r^{\star}\;\lesssim\;\hat{r}_{\text{judge}}-0.10," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mtext>sub</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">≲</mo><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><mo rspace="0.558em">≲</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mtext>judge</mtext></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>0.10</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\hat{r}_{\text{sub}}+0.05\;\lesssim\;r^{\star}\;\lesssim\;\hat{r}_{\text{judge}}-0.10,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where the <math id="A4.SS3.SSS5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.05</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.05</annotation></semantics></math> correction collects genuine opposite-task and keyword-list misses, and the <math id="A4.SS3.SSS5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.10" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.10</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.10</annotation></semantics></math> correction collects the calibrated judge over-fires (using the lower end of the 95% CI to be conservative).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A4.SS3.SSS6" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">D.3.6 </span>Why we report substring matching as the primary metric</h4>

<div id="A4.SS3.SSS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We adopt substring matching as the headline non-refusal metric for harmful prompts on three grounds. First, the bracketing in Eq. <a href="#A4.E10" title="Equation 10 ‣ D.3.5 Bracketing the true refusal rate ‣ D.3 Substring matching vs. LLM judge ‣ Appendix D LLM-as-a-judge: protocol, behavioural decomposition, and comparison with substring matching ‣ Refusal Beyond a Single Direction: A Preliminary Comparison of Diff-in-Means and INLP" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a> shows that the substring-measured rate is closer to <math id="A4.SS3.SSS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>r</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> than the raw judge rate. Second, the <math id="A4.SS3.SSS6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim 5" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>∼</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim 5</annotation></semantics></math> p.p. correction is a property of the prompt set rather than of the model or intervention, so the <em id="A4.SS3.SSS6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">relative</em> ordering of methods under substring matching coincides with the ordering under the calibrated metric: comparisons between methods are unaffected. Third, substring matching is deterministic, reproducible, and directly comparable to <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Arditi et al. (2024)</a></cite> and the broader refusal-direction literature. We use the LLM judge as a complementary diagnostic: its structured outputs (<span id="A4.SS3.SSS6.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">initial_refusal_then_compliance</span>, <span id="A4.SS3.SSS6.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">request_satisfied</span>, <span id="A4.SS3.SSS6.p1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">refusing_opposite_task</span>, <span id="A4.SS3.SSS6.p1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">is_looping_or_repetitive</span>) are far more informative than its binary refusal label, and surface qualitative differences between methods that the headline metrics cannot see.</p>
</div>
<div id="A4.SS3.SSS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS3.SSS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Here are some practical considerations we suggest to keep in mind when using a judge model in refusal experiments:</p>
<ol id="A4.I2" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A4.I2.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A4.I2.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I2.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I2.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Mitigate taboo-topic over-fire.</span> A second judging pass that consumes only the response (without the prompt) and asks “does the response itself materially advance some task, irrespective of what the user asked?” would remove prompt-conditioning of the judge.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I2.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A4.I2.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I2.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I2.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Augment the substring keyword list</span> with the non-canonical refusal phrasings exposed in bucket 1 (<span id="A4.I2.i2.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">“the premise of the question is…”</span>, <span id="A4.I2.i2.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">“it is not appropriate to…”</span>). This closes most of the bucket-1 gap at zero inference cost.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I2.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A4.I2.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I2.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I2.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Add an opposite-task detection pass.</span> A small classifier trained on the judge’s <span id="A4.I2.i3.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">refusing_opposite_task</span> examples could be applied without paying full LLM-as-judge cost at every evaluation.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I2.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="A4.I2.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I2.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I2.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Use the judge’s structured outputs</span> in headline tables, not just its binary refusal label.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A4.I2.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="A4.I2.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.I2.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A4.I2.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Re-run the audit with a stronger judge.</span> Taboo-topic over-fire plausibly correlates with the judge model’s own refusal training; a more capable judge might exhibit a smaller positive bias on bucket 3, narrowing the bracketing in Eq. <a href="#A4.E10" title="Equation 10 ‣ D.3.5 Bracketing the true refusal rate ‣ D.3 Substring matching vs. LLM judge ‣ Appendix D LLM-as-a-judge: protocol, behavioural decomposition, and comparison with substring matching ‣ Refusal Beyond a Single Direction: A Preliminary Comparison of Diff-in-Means and INLP" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>All results tables</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This appendix reports the full experimental grid underlying Table <a href="#S4.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ Models. ‣ 4 Experimental setup ‣ Refusal Beyond a Single Direction: A Preliminary Comparison of Diff-in-Means and INLP" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. The grid varies along two axes.</p>
</div>
<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Application scope.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Interventions are applied either only at the selected component <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(l,t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(l,t)</annotation></semantics></math>, as in the main paper (Tables <a href="#A5.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ 𝑘-regime. ‣ Appendix E All results tables ‣ Refusal Beyond a Single Direction: A Preliminary Comparison of Diff-in-Means and INLP" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a>–<a href="#A5.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ 𝑘-regime. ‣ Appendix E All results tables ‣ Refusal Beyond a Single Direction: A Preliminary Comparison of Diff-in-Means and INLP" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>), or at every layer and token position, following <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Arditi et al. (2024)</a></cite> (Tables <a href="#A5.T10" title="Table 10 ‣ 𝑘-regime. ‣ Appendix E All results tables ‣ Refusal Beyond a Single Direction: A Preliminary Comparison of Diff-in-Means and INLP" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>–<a href="#A5.T13" title="Table 13 ‣ 𝑘-regime. ‣ Appendix E All results tables ‣ Refusal Beyond a Single Direction: A Preliminary Comparison of Diff-in-Means and INLP" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">13</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h5 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph"><math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>-regime.</h5>

<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The size of the erased subspace is set to <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=n</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=1</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=k_{0.9}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>0.9</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=k_{0.9}</annotation></semantics></math>, or <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=k_{0.8}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>0.8</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=k_{0.8}</annotation></semantics></math>, as defined in Section <a href="#S3.SS5" title="3.5 Selecting layer and token position ‣ 3 Methods ‣ Refusal Beyond a Single Direction: A Preliminary Comparison of Diff-in-Means and INLP" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.5</span></a>. Directional ablation and the ActAdd variants do not depend on <math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>; their rows are therefore identical across the four tables of a given scope, and are repeated so that each table supports a self-contained comparison.</p>
</div>
<div id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ Models. ‣ 4 Experimental setup ‣ Refusal Beyond a Single Direction: A Preliminary Comparison of Diff-in-Means and INLP" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> in the main paper is drawn from Tables <a href="#A5.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ 𝑘-regime. ‣ Appendix E All results tables ‣ Refusal Beyond a Single Direction: A Preliminary Comparison of Diff-in-Means and INLP" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> (<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=n</annotation></semantics></math>) and <a href="#A5.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ 𝑘-regime. ‣ Appendix E All results tables ‣ Refusal Beyond a Single Direction: A Preliminary Comparison of Diff-in-Means and INLP" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> (<math id="A5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=k_{0.8}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>0.8</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=k_{0.8}</annotation></semantics></math>), with MMLU/ARC and the perplexity columns averaged.</p>
</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 10: </span>All experiments — every layer, <math id="A5.T10.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=n</annotation></semantics></math>. Values are <math id="A5.T10.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> from baseline, oriented so that higher is better; <math id="A5.T10.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> denotes
SE for effectiveness columns and SD for performance columns. PPL deltas use median
per-example perplexity; SDs above <math id="A5.T10.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1000</annotation></semantics></math> are shown as <math id="A5.T10.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gg\!1000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≫</mo><mn>1000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gg\!1000</annotation></semantics></math>.
<em id="A5.T10.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Takeaway:</em> applying at every layer helps DiM (Llama-2 directional ablation
rises from <math id="A5.T10.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.46" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.46</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.46</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A5.T10.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.91" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.91</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.91</annotation></semantics></math>) but destabilises INLP: Gemma’s <math id="A5.T10.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha=2</annotation></semantics></math> cell
records <math id="A5.T10.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.91" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.91</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.91</annotation></semantics></math> non-refusal alongside a <math id="A5.T10.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.05</annotation></semantics></math> unsafety delta and <math id="A5.T10.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-1.00" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1.00</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1.00</annotation></semantics></math>
perplexity on all three corpora — degenerate output that defeats the substring
metric rather than genuine refusal suppression. This asymmetry is why the main
paper restricts interventions to the selected component.</figcaption>

(<math id="A5.T12.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.91" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.91</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.91</annotation></semantics></math> non-refusal against a <math id="A5.T12.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.05" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.05</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.05</annotation></semantics></math> unsafety delta) recurs unchanged, confirming it
is a property of all-layer application rather than of the <math id="A5.T12.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>-regime. Elsewhere the

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 13: </span>All experiments — every layer, <math id="A5.T13.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=k_{0.8}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mn>0.8</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=k_{0.8}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Values are <math id="A5.T13.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> from baseline, oriented so that higher is better; <math id="A5.T13.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> denotes
SE for effectiveness columns and SD for performance columns. PPL deltas use median
per-example perplexity; SDs above <math id="A5.T13.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1000</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1000</annotation></semantics></math> are shown as <math id="A5.T13.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\gg\!1000" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≫</mo><mn>1000</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\gg\!1000</annotation></semantics></math>.
<em id="A5.T13.3" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">Takeaway:</em> the clearest instance of the scope asymmetry. Nullspace projection
improves markedly over its selected-component counterpart
(Table <a href="#A5.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ 𝑘-regime. ‣ Appendix E All results tables ‣ Refusal Beyond a Single Direction: A Preliminary Comparison of Diff-in-Means and INLP" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>) — most strikingly on Llama-2, where it rises
from <math id="A5.T13.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.03" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.03</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.03</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="A5.T13.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.32</annotation></semantics></math> — whereas counterfactual flipping falls on four of five
models. The two INLP interventions therefore prefer opposite application scopes.</figcaption>
